principles: Web source claim is bounded; its publication date, locality and type of observance are retained.
Modern diocesan guidance never retroactively authenticates a particular 1962 Rituale formula.
Historical customs do not create new Holy Day obligations, universal feast ranks, priestly blessings, or implicit procession flags.
No source-only claims are published to the existing Calendar, LIVE Mass, Pray, Saints or Customs Atlas.
No extended quotation from Weiser or third-party books.

witnesses.title: Historical Ember-day priestly intentions, harvest thanksgiving and alms

independent_source.issuer: Catholic Culture, September 2026 overview

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: The source specifically identifies seasonal Ember prayer, fasting, almsgiving, thanksgiving for crops, and petitions for clergy. These are historical 1962-linked meanings, not a current globally binding fast.

witnesses.title: Ember-day prayers for the dead

independent_source.issuer: Catholic Culture, September 2026 overview

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: The source covers seasonal penitence and gratitude but does not substantiate a dedicated Ember prayer custom specifically for deceased souls.

witnesses.title: Family Rogation prayer walks for crops

independent_source.issuer: Mary Reed Newland via Catholic Culture, family liturgical custom

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: An independent Catholic family custom guide explicitly proposes a family walk asking for God's blessing on gardens and fields. A family prayer is distinct from a priest's processional blessing.

witnesses.title: Shrove Tuesday pancake custom

independent_source.issuer: Archdiocese of St Louis excerpt on Catholic Culture

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Pancakes prepared in England/Ireland to use eggs, milk and fat before older penitential food restrictions; not a present legal Lenten requirement.

witnesses.title: Good Friday private silence and reduced food

independent_source.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy, Good Friday

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Good Friday recollection and penitence are supported but the precise household custom of minimal food alongside silence is not independently documented; modern fasting laws need separate jurisdiction/age handling.

witnesses.title: Eucharistic adoration during Corpus Christi processions

independent_source.issuer: Benedict XVI, Corpus Christi homily 22 May 2008

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Public kneeling/adoration accompanying procession confirmed; particular action 'outside one's own home' is not individually verified and must not be asserted.

witnesses.title: Corpus Christi Eucharistic stations and blessing

independent_source.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy, nos. 162–163

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: The directory acknowledges stops at decorated altars on Eucharistic procession routes and solemn benediction at the conclusion; number/form of stations varies locally and is not 1962 rubric-certified by this witness.

witnesses.title: Blessed harvest wreaths and bread at Polish dożynki

independent_source.issuer: Polish Bishops' Conference, 30 August 2015

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Polish episcopal account explicitly reports archbishop blessing harvest wreaths and bread during diocesan/provincial harvest celebration; source confirms a regional ministerial practice, not universal Roman calendar date.

witnesses.title: Crèche display until 2 February Candlemas

independent_source.issuer: Diocese of Paris, La Chandeleur fête de la lumière (2014)

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Diocese explicitly distinguishes the end of liturgical Christmas from the domestic tradition of keeping a Nativity crib until Candlemas; not a universal removal requirement.

witnesses.title: Cleaning graves and placing flowers or lights

independent_source.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety; Polish Bishops' Conference 31 Oct 2025

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Cemetery visits with tending graves, flowers and lamps acknowledged, while Polish bishops confirm local November family candle traditions; no mandatory grave visit or superstitious implications.

witnesses.title: Beans, peas and lentils as All Souls gifts to the poor

independent_source.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety, prayer and alms for dead

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: General almsgiving for the deceased supported, but specific beans/peas/lentils as a named regional food custom not verified.

witnesses.title: St John Baptist bonfires and community prayers

independent_source.issuer: Diocese of Bayonne, Lescar and Oloron, Saint-Jean parish celebration 2026

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: A parish event near 24 June includes Mass, community bonfire, shared meal, songs and prayers; confirms one local celebration, not a church-mandated ceremony or all Breton sea-fire variants.

witnesses.title: Tuesday novenas and devotions to St Anthony

independent_source.issuer: Franciscan Media, St Anthony of Padua traditions

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Franciscan account reports nine or thirteen Tuesday or Sunday devotional cycles at churches and shrines; stories of promised miracles/old indulgences not treated as current guarantees.

witnesses.title: Medieval French pilgrimage to St Anne

independent_source.issuer: Sanctuaire Sainte-Anne-d'Auray, Grand Pardon 2026

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Living Breton Grand Pardon and French devotion documented; does not demonstrate Weiser's specific medieval chronology or extent in France.

witnesses.title: Parish patronal feasts and local processions

independent_source.issuer: Sanctuaire Sainte-Anne-d'Auray, Grand Pardon 2026

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Specific Saint Anne patronal observance with pilgrimage, Mass, local procession and reconciliation; contributes a local example to existing PATR-001, no generalized parish patron calendar.

witnesses.title: Blessed palm at graves or procession through cemetery

independent_source.issuer: Diocese of Paris, Catechetical Lent/Easter family resource

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Blessed branches placed on graves are documented, but cemetery visitation specifically during the Palm Sunday liturgical procession is not verified.

witnesses.title: Forty Hours adoration before Lent

independent_source.issuer: Diocese of Paris, Forty Hours for the Lord (2018)

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Contemporary forty-hour exposition/adoration in Lent documented; historical pre-Lenten carnival timing not established by this source.

witnesses.title: Priestly blessing of graves on All Souls

independent_source.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Community cemetery prayer and visits supported; specific priestly formula for blessing graves is not documented in this witness.

witnesses.title: Corpus Christi flower wreaths on flags and a priest's wreath blessing

independent_source.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety, Corpus Christi procession

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Flowers and procession route decorations are documented, but woven wreaths on banners and a separate priestly wreath blessing have not been independently established.

witnesses.title: St Anne feast as name day for Anne

independent_source.issuer: Sanctuaire Sainte-Anne-d'Auray, Grand Pardon 2026

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: July 26 celebration documented; does not demonstrate baptismal name-day customs for Annes in all French households (already general NDAY-001).

witnesses.title: Breton fishermen St John sea fires

independent_source.issuer: Diocese 64, Oloron bonfire

witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Pyrenean Catholic bonfire documented, but no independent Breton fishing-boat or maritime rite evidence.
